# reco_user (Resource)

Manages a Reco user. The stable identifier is user_id (set after create, never changes). Changing email_address updates the user in place — it does not force a replacement. Import accepts either the email address or the user_id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "reco_user" "alice" {
  email_address = "alice@example.com"
  name          = "Alice Smith"
  user_roles    = [reco_role.soc_analyst.name]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email_address` (String) User email address. Changing this updates the user in place.
- `name` (String) Display name of the user.
- `user_roles` (List of String) Role names assigned to the user. A user must have at least one role.

### Optional

- `enablement_status` (String) User enablement status: enabled, disabled, or invited (invited is read-only).
- `expiration` (String) User expiration timestamp in RFC3339 format. Omit or set to null for no expiration.
- `is_bypass_sso_enforcement` (Boolean) When true, the user can sign in without SSO even when SSO enforcement is enabled.
- `segments` (List of String) List of segment names the user belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `auth_methods` (List of String) Authentication methods active for this user (read-only).
- `creation_time` (String) User creation timestamp (read-only).
- `id` (String) Terraform resource identifier. Equal to user_id.
- `last_login_time` (String) Last login timestamp (read-only).
- `profile_picture_url` (String) Profile picture URL (read-only).
- `user_id` (String) Reco user ID. Stable identifier assigned on creation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = reco_user.alice
  id = "alice@example.com"
}
```
